claim: MAGIC is a novel FRET-based technology for multiplex analysis of gene expression in individual living cells.
source: Herein we describe a novel Förster Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET)-based technology for the multiplex analysis of gene expression in individual living cells (termed MAGIC, patent application pending; Atmanli and Domian, 2016) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states that MAGIC is a novel FRET-based technology for multiplex gene expression analysis in living cells.

claim: MAGIC enables real-time assessment of transcript expression in single living cells.
source: Our technology enables the real-time assessment of transcript expression in single living cells.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this capability of the technology.

claim: MAGIC uses fluorescently labeled mRNA-specific antisense RNA probes and dsRNA-binding protein to identify gene expression via FRET.
source: Our approach utilizes fluorescently labeled mRNA-specific anti-sense RNA probes and dsRNA-binding protein to identify the expression of specific genes in real-time at single-cell resolution via FRET.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the components and mechanism of MAGIC.

claim: MAGIC was used to identify distinct myocardial subpopulations expressing MHCα and MLC2a during early differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells.
source: We use this technology to identify distinct myocardial subpopulations expressing the structural proteins myosin heavy chain α and myosin light chain 2a in real-time during early differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this application of the technology.

claim: MAGIC combines live-cell gene expression analysis with detailed physiologic phenotyping to capture functional evolution of early myocardial subpopulations.
source: We combine this live-cell gene expression analysis with detailed physiologic phenotyping to capture the functional evolution of these early myocardial subpopulations during lineage specification and diversification.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes this combined approach.

claim: Cellular heterogeneity contributes to developmental dynamics of various types of stem cells.
source: Cellular heterogeneity demonstrably contributes to the developmental dynamics of various types of stem cells (Dulken et al., 2017; Kumar et al., 2014; Wilson et al., 2015), neurons (Sandoe and Eggan, 2013) and cancer (Meacham and Morrison, 2013).
evidence: The statement is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Cellular heterogeneity contributes to developmental dynamics of neurons.
source: Cellular heterogeneity demonstrably contributes to the developmental dynamics of various types of stem cells (Dulken et al., 2017; Kumar et al., 2014; Wilson et al., 2015), neurons (Sandoe and Eggan, 2013) and cancer (Meacham and Morrison, 2013).
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.

claim: Cellular heterogeneity contributes to cancer.
source: Cellular heterogeneity demonstrably contributes to the developmental dynamics of various types of stem cells (Dulken et al., 2017; Kumar et al., 2014; Wilson et al., 2015), neurons (Sandoe and Eggan, 2013) and cancer (Meacham and Morrison, 2013).
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.

claim: Multiple cardiac myocyte lineages and sublineages must interact with endothelial cells, smooth muscle cells and cardiac fibroblasts to form the mature four-chambered adult heart.
source: Multiple cardiac myocyte lineages and sublineages, along with endothelial cells, smooth muscle cells and cardiac fibroblasts must interact in a cohesive program to form the mature four-chambered adult heart (Bu et al., 2009; Domian et al., 2009).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Advances in pluripotent stem cell biology open unprecedented avenues for the study of human cellular differentiation, physiology, and pathophysiology in vitro.
source: Advances in pluripotent stem cell (PSC) biology open unprecedented avenues for the study of human cellular differentiation, physiology, and pathophysiology in vitro (Lan et al., 2013) and also underscore the heterogeneity of clinically important cell types (Bryant et al., 1997; Burridge et al., 2014; Cordeiro et al., 2004; Lian et al., 2012).
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.

claim: Advances in pluripotent stem cell biology underscore the heterogeneity of clinically important cell types.
source: Advances in pluripotent stem cell (PSC) biology open unprecedented avenues for the study of human cellular differentiation, physiology, and pathophysiology in vitro (Lan et al., 2013) and also underscore the heterogeneity of clinically important cell types (Bryant et al., 1997; Burridge et al., 2014; Cordeiro et al., 2004; Lian et al., 2012).
evidence: The statement is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Single-cell transcriptional profiling has provided insight into how intracellular signaling is regulated at the single-cell transcriptional level during cardiac development.
source: Single-cell transcriptional profiling initially via multiplex qPCR analysis and more recently via whole transcriptome sequencing has provided insight into how intracellular signaling is regulated at the single-cell transcriptional level during cardiac development (Cui et al., 2019; DeLaughter et al., 2016; Friedman et al., 2018; Li et al., 2016; Sahara et al., 2019).
evidence: The statement is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Whole genome expression analysis does not allow for concurrent physiological assessment of single living cells.
source: Despite this progress, whole genome expression analysis does not allow for concurrent physiological assessment of single living cells and consequently, the functional significance of single-cell transcriptomic heterogeneity remains unclear.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this limitation of whole genome expression analysis.

claim: The functional significance of single-cell transcriptomic heterogeneity remains unclear.
source: Despite this progress, whole genome expression analysis does not allow for concurrent physiological assessment of single living cells and consequently, the functional significance of single-cell transcriptomic heterogeneity remains unclear.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this gap in knowledge.

claim: Live-cell identification of distinct cell populations has most commonly been accomplished with fluorescent reporter proteins under transcriptional control of the gene of interest.
source: The live-cell identification of distinct cell populations has most commonly been accomplished with gene expression assays that rely on the detection of fluorescent reporter proteins under the transcriptional control of the gene of interest.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this common approach.

claim: Fluorescent reporter protein approaches require generation of transgenic animals or embryonic stem cell lines.
source: Accordingly, these approaches require the generation of transgenic animals (Domian et al., 2009; Wu et al., 2006) or embryonic stem cell lines (Elliott et al., 2011; Klug et al., 1996) to isolate and study discrete subsets of cells with specific gene expression profiles.
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Fluorescent reporter protein methods are cumbersome, time consuming, and expensive.
source: These methods are cumbersome, time consuming, and expensive and therefore allow for only a limited number of genes to be examined at a time.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states these limitations.

claim: Technical advances have facilitated live-cell mRNA imaging by detecting gene transcripts via nucleic acid or protein probes.
source: Technical advances have facilitated live-cell mRNA imaging by detecting gene transcripts via nucleic acid (Santangelo et al., 2009; Tyagi and Kramer, 1996; Vargas et al., 2011) or protein probes (Bertrand et al., 1998; Nelles et al., 2016; Ozawa et al., 2007).
evidence: The statement is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Existing live-cell mRNA imaging techniques have drawbacks including genetic encoding requirements, necessity to target multiple binding sites, complexity of probe design and cellular delivery, and low sensitivity.
source: However, several drawbacks of these existing techniques such as genetic encoding of target mRNA and reporter protein, the necessity to target multiple binding sites, complexity of probe design and cellular delivery and low sensitivity (Armitage, 2011; Tyagi, 2009) have prevented their widespread use (Table 1).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations and reference to Table 1.

claim: MAGIC Factor is the recombinant dsRNA-binding domain of human protein kinase R that has been fluorescently labeled.
source: MAGIC Factor is the recombinant dsRNA-binding domain of human protein kinase R that has been fluorescently labeled and affinity purified against dsRNA.
evidence: The statement is explicitly described in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: MAGIC Probes are generated by in vitro transcription using T7 phage polymerase and fluorescently-labeled using aminoallyl-modified UTP nucleotides.
source: MAGIC anti-sense RNA Probes are generated by in vitro transcription using T7 phage polymerase and fluorescently-labeled using aminoallyl-modified UTP nucleotides.
evidence: The statement is explicitly described in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Upon cellular delivery, MAGIC Probes hybridize to their target gene and generate an RNA-RNA duplex.
source: Upon cellular delivery, MAGIC Probes hybridize to their target gene and generate an RNA-RNA duplex.
evidence: The statement is explicitly described in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: MAGIC Factor binds to the dsRNA formed by MAGIC Probe hybridization, bringing donor and acceptor fluorophores into close contact for FRET to occur.
source: This enables MAGIC Factor to bind to the newly formed dsRNA, thereby bringing the donor fluorophore on the protein to come into close contact with the acceptor fluorophore on the RNA probe and for FRET to occur (blue arrow: excitation of the donor; green arrow: energy transfer; red arrow: emission of the acceptor).
evidence: The statement is explicitly described in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Cells expressing the gene of interest are identified by assaying the FRET signal.
source: Cells expressing the gene of interest are identified by assaying the FRET signal.
evidence: The statement is explicitly described in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Affinity purification of fluorescent MAGIC Factor restores its binding affinity.
source: Affinity purification of fluorescent MAGIC Factor restores its binding affinity.
evidence: The statement is explicitly described in the text and demonstrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Affinity purification of MAGIC Factor resulted in a 30-fold increase in binding affinity to dsRNA.
source: Affinity purification of MAGIC Factor resulted in a 30-fold increase in binding affinity to dsRNA.
evidence: The statement is explicitly described in the text and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The dsRNA-binding domain of PKR consists of two dsRNA-binding motifs encompassing amino acids 1–169.
source: The dsRBD of PKR consists of two dsRNA-binding motifs encompassing amino acids 1–169 and binds to dsRNA with similar efficiency as the full-size parent protein (Cosentino et al., 1995; Green and Mathews, 1992).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: The dsRNA-binding domain of PKR binds to dsRNA with similar efficiency as the full-size parent protein.
source: The dsRBD of PKR consists of two dsRNA-binding motifs encompassing amino acids 1–169 and binds to dsRNA with similar efficiency as the full-size parent protein (Cosentino et al., 1995; Green and Mathews, 1992).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: The dsRNA-binding domain of PKR exerts a specific interaction with dsRNA with no appreciable binding to dsDNA, ssDNA, ssRNA or RNA-DNA hybrids.
source: It exerts a specific interaction with dsRNA with no appreciable binding to dsDNA, ssDNA, ssRNA or RNA-DNA hybrids (Bevilacqua and Cech, 1996; Nallagatla and Bevilacqua, 2008; Patel et al., 2012).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: The dsRNA-binding domain of PKR interaction with dsRNA is sequence-independent.
source: This interaction is sequence-independent and requires a minimum of 18–20 bp of dsRNA to achieve a robust interaction (Bevilacqua and Cech, 1996; Ucci et al., 2007).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: The dsRNA-binding domain of PKR requires a minimum of 18–20 bp of dsRNA to achieve a robust interaction.
source: This interaction is sequence-independent and requires a minimum of 18–20 bp of dsRNA to achieve a robust interaction (Bevilacqua and Cech, 1996; Ucci et al., 2007).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: One- and two-labeled MAGIC Probes are optimal for in vitro live-cell FRET imaging.
source: Based on these results, we determined that one- and two-labeled MAGIC Probes are optimal for in vitro live-cell FRET imaging.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1E-H.

claim: Over-labeling of MAGIC Probes results in fluorescence quenching.
source: We found a marked difference in the resulting fluorescence intensity between the differently labeled RNA probes, suggesting that over-labeling of MAGIC Probes results in fluorescence quenching (Figure 1F).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Four-labeled RNA exhibited significantly reduced hybridization kinetics at 37°C.
source: When we hybridized the fluorescent RNA to its complementary RNA at 37°C, we found that only the four-labeled RNA exhibited significantly reduced hybridization kinetics Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: MAGIC technology provides a robust FRET signal compared to a control probe when targeting β-actin mRNA in hPSC-CMs.
source: Using our optimized transfection protocol, we delivered a novel β-actin MAGIC Probe along with MAGIC Factor into hPSC-CMs and found that our technology provides a robust FRET signal compared to a control probe that did not have an intracellular target (Figure 2A).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Two different phenotypes of β-actin mRNA localization were found in hPSC-CMs: cells with cytoplasmic distribution and cells with nuclear localization.
source: Intriguingly, we found two different phenotypes of the β-actin mRNA localization in hPSC-CMs: cells with cytoplasmic distribution and cells with nuclear localization of the mRNA (Figure 2A).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The β-actin mRNA is predominantly localized to the cytoplasm in various cell lines.
source: Of note, a number of studies have previously shown in a variety of cell lines that the β-actin mRNA is predominantly localized to the cytoplasm (Ben-Ari et al., 2010; Buxbaum et al., 2014; Femino et al., 1998; Santangelo et al., 2009).
evidence: The statement is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: The MAGIC FRET signal co-localized with the smFISH signal in all cell types examined.
source: Importantly, the MAGIC FRET signal co-localized with the smFISH signal in all cell types examined, as shown by the Manders' Overlap Coefficient (MOC).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: There was a strong correlation between smFISH signal intensity and MAGIC FRET signal intensity in fixed cells.
source: As shown in Figure 2D, there was a strong correlation between the two fluorescent assays.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: A positive correlation was found between MAGIC in living cells and smFISH in the same cells after fixation.
source: We then performed MAGIC on β-actin in living cells first, then fixed and performed smFISH on the same cells. Again we found a positive correlation between the two assays, suggesting that the intensity of FRET signals in MAGIC probes can be used to infer relative gene expression levels.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The intensity of FRET signals in MAGIC probes can be used to infer relative gene expression levels.
source: Again we found a positive correlation between the two assays, suggesting that the intensity of FRET signals in MAGIC probes can be used to infer relative gene expression levels.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing correlation between MAGIC and smFISH.

claim: Co-transfection of MAGIC Probes and MAGIC Factor did not alter cell viability.
source: Finally, we showed that co-transfection of MAGIC Probes and MAGIC Factor did not alter cell viability, target mRNA levels, or target protein levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), consistent with previous reports that unmodified RNAs result in no significant RNA interference and translation inhibition by steric hindrance (Kole et al., 2012).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and supported by citation.

claim: Co-transfection of MAGIC Probes and MAGIC Factor did not alter target mRNA levels.
source: Finally, we showed that co-transfection of MAGIC Probes and MAGIC Factor did not alter cell viability, target mRNA levels, or target protein levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), consistent with previous reports that unmodified RNAs result in no significant RNA interference and translation inhibition by steric hindrance (Kole et al., 2012).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and supported by citation.

claim: Co-transfection of MAGIC Probes and MAGIC Factor did not alter target protein levels.
source: Finally, we showed that co-transfection of MAGIC Probes and MAGIC Factor did not alter cell viability, target mRNA levels, or target protein levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), consistent with previous reports that unmodified RNAs result in no significant RNA interference and translation inhibition by steric hindrance (Kole et al., 2012).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and supported by citation.

claim: Transcript levels of MLC2a and MHCα increase during early cardiac differentiation of hPSC.
source: Prior work from a number of laboratories demonstrated that transcript levels of myosin light chain 2a (MLC2a) and myosin heavy chain α (MHCα) increase during early cardiac differentiation of hPSC (Burridge et al., 2014; Lian et al., 2012), suggesting a key role for both structural proteins for proper development of cardiac contractile function.
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: MHCα and MLC2a are expressed sequentially during hPSC differentiation toward the cardiac lineage, resulting in MHCα+/MLC2a+ and MHCα+/MLC2a- hPSC-CMs.
source: We found that MHCα and MLC2a are expressed sequentially, resulting in MHCα+/MLC2a+ and MHCα+/MLC2a- hPSC-CMs (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: By day 15 of differentiation, the vast majority of hPSC-CMs were co-expressing MHCα and MLC2a.
source: Intriguingly, we found that while by day 15 the vast majority of hPSC-CMs were co-expressing MHCα+ and MLC2a+, no cardiac myocyte expressed MLC2a without also co-expressing MHCα at any time.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: No cardiac myocyte expressed MLC2a without also co-expressing MHCα at any time during differentiation.
source: Intriguingly, we found that while by day 15 the vast majority of hPSC-CMs were co-expressing MHCα+ and MLC2a+, no cardiac myocyte expressed MLC2a without also co-expressing MHCα at any time.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: There is significant batch-to-batch variability in the co-expression of MHCα and MLC2a proteins.
source: Of important note, we also found a significant degree of batch-to-batch variability in the co-expression of these proteins (Figure 3B), further underscoring the importance of live-cell lineage assignment in real-time.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: MLC2v expression commences at day 15 of differentiation and significantly increases as differentiation continues.
source: We found that MLC2v expression commences at day 15 of differentiation and significantly increases as differentiation continues (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The expression of MLC2a starts to decrease beginning at day 15 of differentiation.
source: Concomitantly, the expression of MLC2a starts to decrease beginning at day 15, leaving a mixed population of cells consisting of MLC2a+/MLC2v+, MLC2a+/MLC2v- and MLC2a-/MLC2v+ hPSC-CMs at day 40 of differentiation.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: At day 40 of differentiation, there is a mixed population of cells consisting of MLC2a+/MLC2v+, MLC2a+/MLC2v- and MLC2a-/MLC2v+ hPSC-CMs.
source: Concomitantly, the expression of MLC2a starts to decrease beginning at day 15, leaving a mixed population of cells consisting of MLC2a+/MLC2v+, MLC2a+/MLC2v- and MLC2a-/MLC2v+ hPSC-CMs at day 40 of differentiation.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: MLC2a and MLC2v were exclusively expressed in MHCα+ cells.
source: Of important note, these two markers were exclusively expressed in MHCα+ cells and there were no hPSC-CMs that did not express either MLC2a or MLC2v at any time.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental observations from the study.

claim: There were no hPSC-CMs that did not express either MLC2a or MLC2v at any time.
source: Of important note, these two markers were exclusively expressed in MHCα+ cells and there were no hPSC-CMs that did not express either MLC2a or MLC2v at any time.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental observations from the study.

claim: During early differentiation cardiac myocytes are yet unspecified with respect to cardiac chambers, as shown by the lack of MLC2v expression until day 15 of differentiation.
source: Our results demonstrate that during early differentiation cardiac myocytes are yet unspecified with respect to cardiac chambers, as shown by the lack of MLC2v expression until day 15 of differentiation.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing MLC2v expression timing.

claim: The expression of MHCα and MLC2a is not sufficient to deduce chamber specificity.
source: Further, our data suggest that the expression of MHCα and MLC2a is not sufficient to deduce chamber specificity, in line with previous transcriptomic analysis of the developing human heart (van den Berg et al., 2015).
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data and supported by citation.

claim: During early cardiac differentiation up to day 15, cells do not increase in their size as they differentially express MHCα and MLC2a.
source: Intriguingly, we found that during early cardiac differentiation up to day 15 cells do not increase in their size as they differentially express MHCα and MLC2a (Figure 3E).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Later in differentiation, the expression of MLC2v is accompanied with an increase in cell size.
source: In contrast later in differentiation, the expression of MLC2v is accompanied with an increase in cell size consistent with prior reports that ventricular cardiac myocytes are larger than atrial cardiac myocytes (Campbell et al., 1987).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3E and supported by citation.

claim: Ventricular cardiac myocytes are larger than atrial cardiac myocytes.
source: In contrast later in differentiation, the expression of MLC2v is accompanied with an increase in cell size consistent with prior reports that ventricular cardiac myocytes are larger than atrial cardiac myocytes (Campbell et al., 1987).
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.

claim: MHCα+ hPSC-CMs possess faster spontaneous Ca2+ kinetics than MHCα- hPSC-CMs.
source: Using the live-cell mRNA imaging system, we were able to show that MHCα+ hPSC-CMs possess faster spontaneous Ca2+ kinetics and in particular the ability to shuttle free calcium faster between contraction cycles (Figure 3F).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: MHCα+ hPSC-CMs have the ability to shuttle free calcium faster between contraction cycles than MHCα- hPSC-CMs.
source: Using the live-cell mRNA imaging system, we were able to show that MHCα+ hPSC-CMs possess faster spontaneous Ca2+ kinetics and in particular the ability to shuttle free calcium faster between contraction cycles (Figure 3F).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: hPSC-CMs expressing MHCα exhibited a significantly stronger calcium influx into the cytoplasm in response to caffeine than MHCα- hPSC-CMs.
source: We then tested the effect of caffeine, a sensitizer of ryanodine receptors on the sarcoplasmic reticulum, on these cardiac subpopulations and found that hPSC-CMs expressing MHCα exhibited a significantly stronger calcium influx into the cytoplasm in response to caffeine than MHCα- hPSC-CMs (Figure 3G).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: MHCα+ cardiac myocytes possess relatively more mature contractile apparatus than MHCα- cardiac myocytes.
source: These results show that MHCα+ cardiac myocytes possess relatively more mature contractile apparatus than MHCα- cardiac myocytes, consistent with previous reports that older, more mature cardiac myocytes exhibit faster Ca2+ kinetics (Satin et al., 2008).
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data and supported by citation.

claim: Older, more mature cardiac myocytes exhibit faster Ca2+ kinetics.
source: These results show that MHCα+ cardiac myocytes possess relatively more mature contractile apparatus than MHCα- cardiac myocytes, consistent with previous reports that older, more mature cardiac myocytes exhibit faster Ca2+ kinetics (Satin et al., 2008).
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.

claim: Early cardiac cellular differentiation is accompanied by increased expression of MHCα.
source: Our findings are consistent with previous reports showing that early cardiac cellular differentiation is accompanied by increased expression of MHCα, further corroborating the validity of our approach (Bizy et al., 2013; Piccini et al., 2015).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: MAGIC can detect the same transcriptional dynamics of differentiating cells as smFISH.
source: Strikingly, using our technology, we were able to detect the same transcriptional dynamics of differentiating cells as using smFISH, demonstrating that our approach can be utilized to detect mRNA at the onset of transcription when they are present at less abundant levels.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: MAGIC can be utilized to detect mRNA at the onset of transcription when they are present at less abundant levels.
source: Strikingly, using our technology, we were able to detect the same transcriptional dynamics of differentiating cells as using smFISH, demonstrating that our approach can be utilized to detect mRNA at the onset of transcription when they are present at less abundant levels.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing detection of MHCα at different differentiation stages.

claim: MAGIC enables the study of individual cells at different stages of cellular differentiation.
source: Further, we show that our technology enables the study of individual cells at different stages of cellular differentiation.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing detection across differentiation stages.

claim: There is a robust positive correlation between smFISH/cell and FRET/cell intensities for MHCα and MLC2a.
source: Quantification of the FRET per cell and smFISH per cell intensities revealed not only a strong correlation between these two parameters but also a wide range of transcriptional activity of the MHCα and MLC2a genes in hPSC-CMs that MAGIC was able detect, demonstrating that our technology is suited for the single-cell analysis of heterogeneous cell populations.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: MAGIC was able to detect a wide range of transcriptional activity of the MHCα and MLC2a genes in hPSC-CMs.
source: Quantification of the FRET per cell and smFISH per cell intensities revealed not only a strong correlation between these two parameters but also a wide range of transcriptional activity of the MHCα and MLC2a genes in hPSC-CMs that MAGIC was able detect, demonstrating that our technology is suited for the single-cell analysis of heterogeneous cell populations.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: MAGIC is suited for the single-cell analysis of heterogeneous cell populations.
source: Quantification of the FRET per cell and smFISH per cell intensities revealed not only a strong correlation between these two parameters but also a wide range of transcriptional activity of the MHCα and MLC2a genes in hPSC-CMs that MAGIC was able detect, demonstrating that our technology is suited for the single-cell analysis of heterogeneous cell populations.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing detection of transcriptional heterogeneity.

claim: FRET signals co-localize with smFISH signals for MHCα and MLC2a.
source: Further, we were again able to show that FRET signals co-localize with smFISH signals, as shown by a highly localized FRET and smFISH fluorescence pattern as well as a computational pixel-by-pixel analysis (MOC) (Figure 4C).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The transcription factor NKX2-5 plays a central role during cardiac cellular differentiation.
source: Because the transcription factor NKX2-5 plays a central role during cardiac cellular differentiation (Wu et al., 2006), we made unique MAGIC Probes against the NKX2-5 mRNA.
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.

claim: When using a set of three different probes, the NKX2-5 mRNA can be visualized in single living cells using MAGIC.
source: We first tested whether our technology enables the detection of lower abundant transcripts, such as the ones from transcription factors, and found that when using a set of three different probes the NKX2-5 mRNA can be visualized in single living cells using MAGIC (Figure 5A).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Using MAGIC, the transcriptional dynamics of the longitudinal expression of NKX2-5 in differentiating hPSCs can be replicated as compared with conventional quantitative PCR.
source: Strikingly, using MAGIC we were able to replicate the transcriptional dynamics of the longitudinal expression of NKX2-5 in differentiating hPSCs as compared with conventional quantitative PCR (Figure 5D).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5B-D.

claim: MAGIC enables the detection of low-copy mRNA, such as the ones from transcription factors.
source: Taken together, our data show that MAGIC not only enables the detection of low-copy mRNA, such as the ones from transcription factors, but also to analyze the transcriptional dynamics of transcription factors during developmental processes.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing detection of NKX2-5.

claim: MAGIC enables analysis of the transcriptional dynamics of transcription factors during developmental processes.
source: Taken together, our data show that MAGIC not only enables the detection of low-copy mRNA, such as the ones from transcription factors, but also to analyze the transcriptional dynamics of transcription factors during developmental processes.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing NKX2-5 expression across differentiation stages.

claim: Spectral imaging allows resolution of fluorophores with close spectra in cellular assays.
source: We next tested the suitability of spectral imaging to resolve fluorophores with close spectra in cellular assays and found that it provides a robust method to differentiate between Alexa Fluor 546 and 594, as shown by immunofluorescence staining of the nuclearly located NKX2-5 and the cytoplasmically located MHCα proteins with these fluorophores (Figure 6—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Spectral imaging provides a robust method to differentiate between Alexa Fluor 546 and 594.
source: We next tested the suitability of spectral imaging to resolve fluorophores with close spectra in cellular assays and found that it provides a robust method to differentiate between Alexa Fluor 546 and 594, as shown by immunofluorescence staining of the nuclearly located NKX2-5 and the cytoplasmically located MHCα proteins with these fluorophores (Figure 6—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Using spectral imaging, FRET signals from three FRET pairs can be faithfully resolved from other fluorescence signals in single living cells.
source: Furthermore using spectral imaging, we were able to faithfully resolve the FRET signals from other fluorescence signals in single living cells.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6C and supplementary figures.

claim: Multiplex RNA co-transfection approach yielded a 97% efficiency of the delivery of all three probes into individual cells.
source: Importantly, we found that multiplex RNA co-transfection approach yielded a 97% efficiency of the delivery of all three probes into individual cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2H.

claim: MAGIC was used to identify distinct cardiac lineages based on the expression of MLC2a, NKX2-5 and MHCα in single living hPSC-CMs.
source: Finally to demonstrate the multiplex potential of our technology, we delivered the MLC2a, NKX2-5 and MHCα MAGIC Probes into single living hPSC-CMs and identified distinct cardiac lineages based on the expression of these three genes (Figure 6D).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The co-delivery of MAGIC Factor and three distinct MAGIC probes does not alter cell viability.
source: We further showed that the co-delivery of MAGIC Factor and three distinct MAGIC probes does not alter cell viability (Figure 6E) or mRNA levels (Figure 6F).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The co-delivery of MAGIC Factor and three distinct MAGIC probes does not alter mRNA levels.
source: We further showed that the co-delivery of MAGIC Factor and three distinct MAGIC probes does not alter cell viability (Figure 6E) or mRNA levels (Figure 6F).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: MAGIC coupled with spectral imaging provides a powerful tool for the multiplex imaging of at least three gene pairs in single living cells.
source: Taken together, MAGIC coupled with spectral imaging provides a powerful tool for the multiplex imaging of at least three genes pairs in single living cells and for the study of the processes of lineage commitment and diversification in single living cells.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing multiplex detection.

claim: MAGIC coupled with spectral imaging provides a powerful tool for the study of the processes of lineage commitment and diversification in single living cells.
source: Taken together, MAGIC coupled with spectral imaging provides a powerful tool for the multiplex imaging of at least three genes pairs in single living cells and for the study of the processes of lineage commitment and diversification in single living cells.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing lineage identification.

claim: MAGIC utilizes a hybrid approach comprising fluorescent RNA probes and dsRNA-binding protein to enable FRET to discern hybridized probes within single living cells.
source: Our strategy utilizes a hybrid approach comprising fluorescent RNA probes and dsRNA-binding protein to enable FRET to discern hybridized probes within single living cells.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the hybrid approach of MAGIC.

claim: MAGIC was used to assess the cell physiology of distinct myocardial sublineages during early cardiac differentiation from hPSC.
source: We were able to assess the cell physiology of distinct myocardial sublineages during early cardiac differentiation from hPSC.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this application.

claim: MAGIC was used to study how the transcriptional activation of MHCα impacts the calcium handling capacity of hPSC-CMs.
source: To delineate the process of functional maturation in human cardiac myocytes, we studied how the transcriptional activation of a key contractility protein, MHCα, impacts the calcium handling capacity of hPSC-CMs.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this application.

claim: MAGIC has the broader potential to study how the expression of specific genes regulates single-cell physiology.
source: This approach has the broader potential to study how the expression of specific genes regulates single-cell physiology.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this potential application.

claim: It is increasingly important to validate the functional relevance of lineage-specific markers by single-cell functional assays.
source: As more single-cell transcriptional profiling and related technologies identify new candidate lineage-specific markers, it is increasingly important to validate the functional relevance of these markers by single-cell functional assays, such as the one presented herein.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this need.

claim: Pronounced cell-to-cell variation with respect to morphology and function is evident within multiple tissues and cell types.
source: Pronounced cell-to-cell variation with respect to morphology and function is evident within multiple tissues and cell types, such as stem cells (Dulken et al., 2017; Kumar et al., 2014; Wilson et al., 2015), cardiac myocytes (Bryant et al., 1997; Bu et al., 2009; Cordeiro et al., 2004; Domian et al., 2009), neurons (Sandoe and Eggan, 2013) and various types of tumors (Meacham and Morrison, 2013).
evidence: The statement is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Understanding the cellular processes underlying lineage commitment, lineage diversification, and functional maturation requires the concurrent assessment of transcriptional and functional changes at single-cell resolution.
source: Understanding the cellular processes underlying lineage commitment, lineage diversification, and functional maturation requires the concurrent assessment of transcriptional and functional changes at single-cell resolution.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this requirement.

claim: MAGIC imaging technology could complement existing single-cell assays to further understanding of how transcriptional variation between single cells translates into functional differences.
source: Our imaging technology could therefore complement existing single-cell assays to further our understanding of how transcriptional variation between single cells translates into functional differences.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this potential application.

claim: In multiple transformed cell lines the β-actin mRNA is largely localized to the cytoplasm with little nuclear presence.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that in multiple transformed cell lines the β-actin mRNA is largely localized to the cytoplasm with little nuclear presence (Ben-Ari et al., 2010; Buxbaum et al., 2014; Femino et al., 1998; Nelles et al., 2016; Santangelo et al., 2009).
evidence: The statement is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Nuclear translocation of the β-actin mRNA might play an important role for normal cell function.
source: At the same time, a number of studies have suggested that nuclear translocation of the β-actin mRNA might play an important role for normal cell function (Fallini et al., 2016; Smith et al., 2015).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: A fraction of hPSC-derived cardiac myocytes retained the β-actin mRNA in the nucleus.
source: Concomitant application of MAGIC with the established smFISH technology confirmed the cytoplasmic nature of the β-actin mRNA in U2OS cells; however, strikingly, we found that a fraction of hPSC-derived cardiac myocytes retained the β-actin mRNA in the nucleus (Figure 2A and C).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2A and C.

claim: Gene expression has previously been shown to be subject to stochastic fluctuations arising from short but intense bursts of transcription.
source: Gene expression has previously been shown to be subject to stochastic fluctuations arising from short but intense bursts of transcription (Dar et al., 2012; Raj et al., 2006).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Compartmentalization of mRNA may provide an option to reduce fluctuations in cytoplasmic mRNA levels and may be considered a mode of gene regulation.
source: Since these bursts can result in profound gene expression noise and thus variations in proteins levels, compartmentalization of mRNA may provide an option to reduce fluctuations in cytoplasmic mRNA levels and may thus be considered a mode of gene regulation (Bahar Halpern et al., 2015).
evidence: The statement is supported by citation and represents speculation about function.

claim: The nuclear retention of the β-actin mRNA may ensure stable β-actin protein levels for the correct alignment of actin filaments during the contractility-dependent organization of actin arrays.
source: Given the imperative role of actin filaments in cardiac myocyte contractility, it is possible that the nuclear retention of the β-actin mRNA ensures stable β-actin protein levels for the correct alignment of actin filaments during the contractility-dependent organization of actin arrays (Skwarek-Maruszewska et al., 2009).
evidence: The statement is speculative and supported by citation.

claim: There is interdependence between cellular maturation and contractility.
source: This possibility is further supported by the interdependence between cellular maturation and contractility (Ribeiro et al., 2015) and given that early PSC-derived cardiac myocytes still undergo the process of cellular maturation (Yang et al., 2014), it is possible that the cells displaying marked nuclear retention of the β-actin mRNA were in the process of organizing their sarcomeric actin structures.
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.

claim: Early PSC-derived cardiac myocytes still undergo the process of cellular maturation.
source: This possibility is further supported by the interdependence between cellular maturation and contractility (Ribeiro et al., 2015) and given that early PSC-derived cardiac myocytes still undergo the process of cellular maturation (Yang et al., 2014), it is possible that the cells displaying marked nuclear retention of the β-actin mRNA were in the process of organizing their sarcomeric actin structures.
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.

claim: MAGIC will be useful for the study of the functional significance of variations in mRNA localization.
source: Given the strength of our technology to provide a spatial resolution of mRNA expression, we anticipate that MAGIC will be useful for the study of the functional significance of variations in mRNA localization.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this anticipated application.

claim: Poorly defined heterogeneous mixtures of cell cultures limit the strength of population studies in PSC disease models of specific cellular subtypes.
source: Poorly defined heterogeneous mixtures of cell cultures limit the strength of population studies in PSC disease models of specific cellular subtypes.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this limitation.

claim: A number of protocols for efficient PSC differentiation toward specific cell types have been established.
source: While a number of protocols for efficient PSC differentiation toward specific cell types have been established (Maroof et al., 2013; Pagliuca et al., 2014; Protze et al., 2017), these enrichment strategies are not well suited to study the dynamics governing cellular sublineages.
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Enrichment strategies for PSC differentiation are not well suited to study the dynamics governing cellular sublineages.
source: While a number of protocols for efficient PSC differentiation toward specific cell types have been established (Maroof et al., 2013; Pagliuca et al., 2014; Protze et al., 2017), these enrichment strategies are not well suited to study the dynamics governing cellular sublineages.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this limitation.

claim: There is an inherent disconnect between how tissue development and pathogenesis occur in vivo and how they are recreated in PSC in vitro models.
source: Hence, there is an inherent disconnect between how tissue development and pathogenesis occur in vivo and how they are recreated in PSC in vitro models.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this disconnect.

claim: Modeling of the biology and disease of specific cell subtypes could be facilitated using MAGIC by targeting specific cellular subsets using validated markers.
source: Modeling of the biology and disease of specific cell subtypes could now be facilitated using MAGIC by targeting specific cellular subsets using validated markers.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this potential application.

claim: Lineage assignment in real-time using MAGIC could potentially be leveraged to select multiple specific cell subtypes by fluorescence activated cell sorting.
source: Further, lineage assignment in real-time using MAGIC could also potentially be leveraged to select multiple specific cell subtypes by fluorescence activated cell sorting, as previously demonstrated using molecular beacon probes (Ban et al., 2013; Jha et al., 2015).
evidence: The statement is speculative and supported by citations to published work.

claim: MAGIC preserves cell viability after cellular delivery of MAGIC components.
source: Our technology preserves cell viability, and mRNA and protein expression after cellular delivery of MAGIC components, which altogether are prerequisites for successful longitudinal studies.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data showing no effect on viability.

claim: MAGIC preserves mRNA expression after cellular delivery of MAGIC components.
source: Our technology preserves cell viability, and mRNA and protein expression after cellular delivery of MAGIC components, which altogether are prerequisites for successful longitudinal studies.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data showing no effect on mRNA levels.

claim: MAGIC preserves protein expression after cellular delivery of MAGIC components.
source: Our technology preserves cell viability, and mRNA and protein expression after cellular delivery of MAGIC components, which altogether are prerequisites for successful longitudinal studies.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data showing no effect on protein levels.

claim: Variable intercellular transfection efficiency may be a limiting factor for MAGIC.
source: Since our technology relies on the delivery of both MAGIC Factor and Probes into the same cell, variable intercellular transfection efficiency may be a limiting factor.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this potential limitation.

claim: Different cell types may be transfected with variable transfection efficiencies.
source: This may further be compounded by the cell type of interest, as different cell types may be transfected with variable transfection efficiencies.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this consideration.

claim: Efficient transfection of MAGIC constructs does not pose a considerable challenge to the general applicability of the technology given the large number of commercially available transfection reagents.
source: Given the large number of commercially available transfection reagents, we do not anticipate that efficient transfection of MAGIC constructs poses a considerable challenge to the general applicability of our technology.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this expectation.

claim: MAGIC technology will be useful for any application where cellular heterogeneity with respect to gene expression and cell physiology plays an important biological role.
source: Collectively, we anticipate that this technology will be useful for any application where cellular heterogeneity with respect to gene expression and cell physiology plays an important biological role.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this anticipated broad applicability.

claim: MHCα and MLC2a mRNA counts are lower than β-actin mRNA counts in single hPSC-CMs.
source: Using specific custom smFISH probes to quantify transcript levels of β-actin, MHCα and MLC2a in single hPSC-CMs we showed that MHCα and MLC2a mRNA counts are lower than β-actin mRNA counts, further demonstrating that our technology can detect lower abundant transcripts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: MAGIC can detect lower abundant transcripts.
source: Using specific custom smFISH probes to quantify transcript levels of β-actin, MHCα and MLC2a in single hPSC-CMs we showed that MHCα and MLC2a mRNA counts are lower than β-actin mRNA counts, further demonstrating that our technology can detect lower abundant transcripts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing detection of MHCα and MLC2a.

claim: The mRNA count of β-actin in hPSC-CMs was consistent with previous reports.
source: The mRNA count of β-actin in hPSC-CMs was consistent with previous reports (Femino et al., 1998; Santangelo et al., 2009).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: MHC proteins have previously been shown to play a critical role for the calcium handling of hPSC-CMs.
source: Since MHC proteins have previously been shown to play a critical role for the calcium handling of hPSC-CMs (Lan et al., 2013), we first investigated how MHCα expression correlates with cardiac myocyte function.
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.

claim: The intracellular delivery of MAGIC Probes and MAGIC Factor did not affect cellular Ca2+ dynamics.
source: The intracellular delivery of MAGIC Probes and MAGIC Factor did not affect cellular Ca2+ dynamics (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: During early cardiac differentiation the step-wise expression of contractile proteins promotes cellular differentiation and function.
source: Our findings show that MHCα+ cardiac myocytes possess developmentally more advanced contractile apparatus than MHCα- cardiac myocytes, demonstrating how during early cardiac differentiation the step-wise expression of contractile proteins promotes cellular differentiation and function.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing functional differences between MHCα+ and MHCα- cells.

claim: The expression of a key player of a cellular differentiation program is directly linked with the functional outcome at single-cell resolution.
source: Taken together, we showed that the expression of a key player of a cellular differentiation program is directly linked with the functional outcome at single-cell resolution.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data linking MHCα expression to calcium handling.

claim: Progression in cellular differentiation is tightly associated with functional evolution.
source: These results demonstrate how progression in cellular differentiation is tightly associated with functional evolution.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing correlation between differentiation stage and function.

claim: Cells progressively increased the expression of MHCα during differentiation from undifferentiated hPSCs to day 20 cardiac myocytes.
source: By quantifying the smFISH fluorescence signals per single cell, we found that cells progressively increased the expression of MHCα during differentiation (Figure 4A).
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Alexa Fluor 488 has a quantum yield of 0.92.
source: Because Alexa Fluor 488 has a quantum yield of 0.92 (Dempsey et al., 2011), we chose to use it as a common donor for all three acceptors used in this study.
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.

claim: In spectral imaging, the entire fluorescence spectrum is acquired upon laser excitation to form a 'lambda stack' consisting of multiple detection windows spanning typically 10–50 nm.
source: In spectral imaging, the entire fluorescence spectrum is acquired upon laser excitation to form a so called 'lambda stack' consisting of multiple detection windows spanning typically 10–50 nm (Zimmermann et al., 2003).
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.

claim: Linear unmixing is based on the assumption that each fluorophore contributes in a linear manner to the fluorescence signal recorded in any given spectral detection channel.
source: This process is based on the assumption that each fluorophore contributes in a linear manner to the fluorescence signal recorded in any given spectral detection channel.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this principle of linear unmixing.

claim: Fluorophores with minute differences in their emission spectra, such as GFP and FITC whose peak emission fluorescence are separated by only 7 nm, can be resolved using spectral imaging.
source: Because all light is collected for determining which fluorophore contributes to every given fluorescence signal, even fluorophores with minute differences in their emission spectra, such as GFP and FITC whose peak emission fluorescence are separated by only 7 nm can be resolved (Haraguchi et al., 2002).
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.

claim: Spectral imaging has been highly validated in both conventional fluorescence and FRET imaging.
source: Spectral imaging has been highly validated in both conventional fluorescence and FRET imaging (Sun et al., 2010; Woehler, 2013; Zimmermann et al., 2003).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: The acceptor bleed-through remained stable with all three acceptors over a large range of fluorescence intensity.
source: Importantly, we found using single-labeled control probes that the acceptor bleed-through remained stable with all three acceptors over a large range of fluorescence intensity (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–D), making the computational removal of spectral-bleedthrough after linear unmixing a reliable method.
evidence: The statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–D.

claim: Computational removal of spectral-bleedthrough after linear unmixing is a reliable method.
source: Importantly, we found using single-labeled control probes that the acceptor bleed-through remained stable with all three acceptors over a large range of fluorescence intensity (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–D), making the computational removal of spectral-bleedthrough after linear unmixing a reliable method.
evidence: The conclusion is based on experimental data showing stable bleed-through.

claim: MLC2a is expressed in all chambers of the developing human heart.
source: Of note, MLC2a is expressed in all chambers of the developing human heart (Chuva de Sousa Lopes et al., 2006; van den Berg et al., 2015).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published work.

claim: MLC2v is a specific ventricular marker in the human heart.
source: To investigate whether the expression of these proteins may confer chamber specificity, we characterized the expression of MHCα and MLC2a together with myosin light chain 2 v (MLC2v), a specific ventricular marker in the human heart (Chuva de Sousa Lopes et al., 2006), during early (up to day 15) and late (up to day 40) differentiation of hPSC.
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to published work.
